name: COSI
unique: A science center on the Scioto with a giant screen theater, a gadget gallery and a working lab where visitors do experiments.
buzz: The hands on labs and the dinosaur gallery are the family stops; the building and the riverfront park are worth the walk.

name: Columbus Museum of Art
unique: A museum with a strong American collection, a sculpture garden and a center for creativity where visitors make things, in a 1931 building.
buzz: The American galleries and the sculpture garden are the route; the hands on center is the family surprise.

name: Findlay Market
unique: The oldest continuously operating public market in the state, in a 1855 iron market house with butchers, a spice shop and a Belgian waffle stand.
buzz: The market is the local Saturday ritual and the surrounding Over the Rhine blocks have changed fast; go early for the produce.

name: Cincinnati Art Museum
unique: A free encyclopedic museum in Eden Park with a strong collection of Old Masters, Asian art and a wing of Cincinnati artists.
buzz: The free admission is the local pride and the ancient galleries are quiet; the park around it is a good walk.

name: Cleveland Museum of Natural History
unique: A museum with a 70 foot titanosaur, a planetarium and a wildlife gallery, recently renovated around a glass atrium.
buzz: The dinosaur hall and the planetarium are the family stops; the museum is on the same campus as the art museum and the botanical garden.

name: Carillon Historical Park
customer: History families, engineering fans, school groups
unique: A park of moved buildings around a carillon, with the 1905 Wright Flyer III, a 1930s print shop and a working brewery.
buzz: The Wright Flyer and the carillon concerts are the reasons to come and the park is bigger than it looks; the brewery pours samples.

name: Dayton Art Institute
unique: A museum on a bluff above the Great Miami with a collection from ancient to American, in a building modeled on the Villa d'Este.
buzz: The building and the American galleries are the reasons to stop; admission is free on some days and the collection is broader than expected.

name: Stan Hywet Hall
unique: A Tudor revival mansion built by the Goodyear founder, with 65 rooms, a Japanese garden and a conservatory, on 70 acres.
buzz: The house and the gardens are the two halves and the holiday lights fill the grounds; the tour is long enough to plan two hours.

name: Pro Football Hall of Fame
unique: The busts of every inducted player in a long gallery, plus a locker room of artifacts and a field where you can run drills.
buzz: The bust gallery is the emotional stop and the interactive field is the family draw; the August enshrinement is the big week.

name: Butler Institute of American Art
unique: The first museum devoted entirely to American art, with a Winslow Homer, a Hopper and a gallery of regional painting, free on the Youngstown State campus.
buzz: The collection is stronger than the city's reputation suggests and it is free; the building is a 1919 marble temple.

name: Museum of Art and Archaeology
unique: A university museum with ancient Greek pottery, a mummy and American painting, free in a building on the Columbia campus.
buzz: The ancient collection is the surprise and the museum is free; it is small and the campus is a pleasant walk.

name: Fantastic Caverns
unique: The only cave in the country you tour by jeep drawn tram, riding through a underground river passage without leaving your seat.
buzz: The ride is the reason children love it and the cave is accessible for people who cannot walk far; the tour is about an hour.

name: Patee House Museum
customer: History families, Pony Express fans, road trippers
unique: A 1858 hotel that was the Pony Express headquarters, now a museum with a railroad, a stagecoach and a recreation of a frontier main street.
buzz: The street scene and the Pony Express story are the reasons to come; it is old fashioned and good with children.

name: Jesse James Home
customer: Outlaw history fans, families, road trippers
unique: The small house where Jesse James was shot in 1882, with the bullet hole in the wall and the story of how his widow sold tours.
buzz: The house is small and the bullet hole is the artifact; it is a quick stop next to the Patee House.

name: Missouri State Capitol
unique: A limestone capitol above the Missouri River with a mural by Thomas Hart Benton in the lounge and a museum on the first floor.
buzz: The Benton mural is the reason art people stop and the view from the river steps is the photograph; tours are free.

name: Jefferson Landing
unique: A restored 1850s river landing with a store and a house built into the levee, where the Santa Fe Trail trade began.
buzz: The buildings and the river view are the stop and it is free; the levee wall itself is the interesting engineering.

name: St. Charles Main Street
unique: A brick main street of 1800s buildings on the Missouri, the first state capital and the start of the Lewis and Clark trail, with a riverfront park.
buzz: The street and the Katy Trail trailhead are the two reasons to come and the shops are touristy; the fall festival is the local event.

name: Rockcliffe Mansion
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 30 room mansion on a bluff above the Mississippi, with original furnishings and a view over Hannibal, left empty for decades and restored.
buzz: The house and the river view are the tour and the story of its abandonment is the interest; it pairs with the Mark Twain sites.

name: Museum of Idaho
unique: A regional museum with a walk through Idaho history, a children's discovery area and traveling exhibits, in a converted warehouse downtown.
buzz: The history walk is good with children and the traveling shows are the reason locals return; it is small and cheap.

name: Hells Gate State Park
company: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation
unique: A park on the Snake River at the lower end of Hells Canyon, where Lewis and Clark came through, with a jet boat launch and a beach.
buzz: The jet boats into Hells Canyon leave from here and the river is the biggest thing in the park; the campground is shaded.

name: Nez Perce National Historical Park
unique: The heart of a park that stretches across four states, with a museum of Nez Perce beadwork, a mission site and the story of the 1877 war.
buzz: The museum and the ranger talks are the reason to start here before following the trail; the collection is from the tribe and the interpretation is theirs.

name: Idaho Museum of Natural History
unique: A museum with a giant short faced bear, a saber tooth cat and the fossils of the Snake River plain, on the Pocatello campus.
buzz: The Ice Age mammals are the family draw and the collection is serious; it is small and cheap.

name: Shoshone Falls
unique: A 212 foot waterfall on the Snake River, taller than Niagara, dropping into a canyon in the middle of the desert.
buzz: The flow is diverted for irrigation and is strongest in spring; the overlook is a short walk and the park has a swimming area below.

name: City of Rocks National Reserve
unique: A field of granite spires where the California Trail passed, now a climbing destination with routes on 600 foot rock and a dark sky.
buzz: Climbers come for the granite cracks and the landscape is strange and quiet; the roads are gravel and the nearest town is small.

name: Minidoka National Historic Site
customer: History people, students, civil rights pilgrims
unique: The remains of a World War II camp where 13,000 Japanese Americans were incarcerated, with a reconstructed barrack, a guard tower and the original root cellar.
buzz: The site is sparse and the stories are the exhibit; rangers lead walks and the isolation is part of the lesson.

name: Sun Valley Museum of Art
unique: A small art museum in Ketchum with contemporary shows, a craft program and a lecture series, free to the public.
buzz: The shows rotate and the museum is the cultural center of the valley; it is free and takes an hour.

name: Sacajawea Interpretive Center
unique: A center on the Lemhi River telling the story of Sacajawea's childhood with the Lemhi Shoshone, with trails along the river and a reconstructed camp.
buzz: The interpretation is from the tribe and the setting is the valley she grew up in; it is a good stop before the Lemhi Pass drive.

name: Payette Lake
unique: A glacial lake ringed by pine and mountains with a town beach, a winter carnival with snow sculptures and a ski hill above it.
buzz: The summer lake and the winter carnival are the two seasons; the town is small and the water is cold and clear.

name: Bruneau Dunes State Park
company: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation
unique: One of the tallest single structure sand dunes in North America at 470 feet, with a lake, a campground and an observatory.
buzz: Sandboarding down the dune is the family fun and the dark sky is the night reason; the sand is hot in summer and the wind is constant.

name: Priest Lake
company: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation
unique: A clear lake in the Selkirk Mountains with huckleberry picking, a state park beach and a road that ends at the Canadian border.
buzz: The lake is quieter than Coeur d'Alene and the water is clear; the drive is long and the nearest town is small.
